agent_note: Heavily dialogue-dominated Goodreads page (16/26) plus 6 gnomic aphorisms -- the source's quotability bias in pure form. Only 4 event quotes, below the >=5 threshold, but all 4 are present and the narration is unambiguously first-person simultaneous: 'My breath catches and my body warms', plus present-tense dialogue tags ('I call after him', 'he answers', 'I scoff') inside q07666, which the quotation-mark-majority rule files as dialogue. Most quotes arrive with quotation marks stripped, so dialogue was identified via vocatives (Violence, Violet, Vi, Liam), second-person address, and imperatives -- signal recorded per quote. No past-tense event narration anywhere in the 26. Flip risk is q07652 ('I am the sky...'), which could be spoken/invoked rather than narrated; it is present either way, so it cannot flip the tense, only the event count (4 -> 3).
